stories.title: Australia: Few Campers, Spread Across the Country
paragraphs: Australia is the only country in Oceania with any campers in the directory. Of its 12 campers, 11 list a usable location, and they come from five of Australia's eight states and territories, in rough proportion to population. The only cluster is small: three campers from Maroubra, in Sydney.
With so few campers, there is little subnational pattern to find. Victoria, home to about a quarter of Australians, has sent one camper.

stories.title: A Small but Steady Trickle Since 1956
paragraphs: Australia's 12 campers span almost the whole history of camp, from 1956 to 2024, but never more than a few per decade. The busiest stretch was 1987–1991, with five campers, three of them from Queensland. Oceania has never supplied more than about 1% of campers in any period.

No other country in Oceania has ever sent a camper. That includes New Zealand (5.3 million people) and Papua New Guinea (10.8 million), along with the Pacific island nations. The main story for Oceania is not a change over time but the need for more campers from across the region.
